The Truth About Storm Chaser Roofing in Lehigh Valley

30 October 2025 Storm Damage

Every fall in the Lehigh Valley, storms sweep across the region, leaving behind wind damage, missing shingles, and desperate homeowners. Right on cue, trucks with out-of-town plates appear, offering quick and cheap repairs. This practice is known as storm chaser roofing, and while it might sound convenient, it often leaves homeowners with poor workmanship, no accountability, and costly repairs later.

At In The Light Roofing, we’ve spent years repairing the damage caused by storm chaser roofing crews. The pattern is always the same: they arrive fast after a storm, make big promises, collect payments, and leave town before issues appear. That’s why knowing the truth about storm chaser roofing is essential for protecting your home.

Why Fall Storms Attract Storm Chaser Roofing Crews

Fall is peak storm season in Pennsylvania. High winds funneling along the Lehigh River, heavy rain systems drifting from Ohio, and even hailstorms like the ones that hit Huron create the perfect conditions for roof damage.

According to NOAA, the Mid-Atlantic frequently sees volatile weather shifts in October and November, when warm days are followed by sudden freezes. These swings crack shingles and loosen flashing. That’s when storm chaser roofing companies flood the region, capitalizing on urgency.

They know homeowners are stressed, worried about leaks, and eager to protect their homes. Unfortunately, that urgency makes families more vulnerable to bad deals.

What Is Storm Chaser Roofing?

Storm chaser roofing refers to contractors who travel from town to town following severe weather events. They’re not local, and their business model depends on high-pressure sales, quick installs, and moving on to the next storm-hit area.

Characteristics of storm chaser roofing companies include:

  • Out-of-state license plates and temporary offices
  • “One-day-only” pricing pressure
  • Requests for large upfront payments
  • Vague or missing warranty coverage
  • Limited or no references in the local community

Unlike established local companies, these crews don’t rely on repeat business, reviews, or reputation. Their goal is to get in, get paid, and get out.

A Local Story from Catasauqua

Last fall, a homeowner in Catasauqua called us after their roof started leaking, just two months after hiring a storm chaser roofing company. The shingles were misaligned, nails were exposed, and flashing wasn’t sealed. When the crew was contacted, their phone number was disconnected.

Our team ended up performing a full tear-off and replacement. The homeowner paid twice, once for the bad job, and once for the fix. They told us, “We just wish we had chosen a local roofer we could trust from the start.”

Why Local Knowledge Matters in Roofing

Lehigh Valley weather is unpredictable. Sudden monsoons like those Ohio systems push across our region, while winter brings freeze-thaw cycles that test every shingle.

Local roofers understand:

  • The types of shingles that hold up against our temperature swings
  • The importance of gutter systems in leafy neighborhoods like Bethlehem and Catasauqua
  • How high winds affect open-field homes in Upper Macungie
  • The risk of ice dams in older slate-roof homes on Allentown’s West End

When you work with a trusted local company, you’re not just hiring for a project, you’re investing in long-term knowledge of how roofs survive in the Lehigh Valley. That’s a benefit storm chaser roofing crews can never provide.

Red Flags of Storm Chaser Roofing

Here’s what our licensed roofers say to watch for:

  • Unmarked trucks with magnetic signs that can be swapped out
  • High-pressure sales tactics, like “sign today for a discount”
  • No physical address in the Lehigh Valley
  • Limited warranty promises that sound too good to be true
  • Large upfront deposits requested before materials are delivered

By contrast, a reputable company like In The Light Roofing offers clear contracts, detailed scopes of work, and proof of insurance.

The Real Cost of Storm Chaser Roofing

At first glance, storm chaser roofing looks cheaper. But hidden costs pile up:

  • Poor installation leads to leaks within months
  • Shingle warranties are voided by improper installs
  • Repairs cost more because damage spreads
  • No local office to hold accountable

In short, saving a few hundred dollars up front often costs thousands later.

Local Example: Bethlehem Township

One Bethlehem Township homeowner shared their experience after hiring a storm chaser roofing crew in fall 2022. The company installed shingles over wet decking, trapping moisture. Within weeks, the attic smelled of mildew. When they tried to call the company, they discovered the roofer had already left Pennsylvania for another storm-hit region.

Our crew replaced the roof properly, ventilated the attic, and documented the project for the homeowner’s records. Stories like this are common in the Lehigh Valley and highlight why trusting local professionals is always safer.

How to Protect Yourself from Storm Chaser Roofing

Here are proactive steps every homeowner should take:

  1. Check for a local address. A reputable roofer will have a permanent office nearby.
  2. Ask for references. Local roofers should be able to provide projects you can actually drive by.
  3. Verify insurance. Confirm they carry liability and workers’ comp insurance.
  4. Look for certifications. Manufacturers like GAF and CertainTeed certify trusted installers.
  5. Don’t rush. Be wary of contractors pushing “sign today” deals.

If you’re uncertain, schedule a trusted local inspection before agreeing to any work.

Building Trust with Local Roofing

At In The Light Roofing, our approach is different. We rely on trust, reviews, and relationships in the community. We’ve installed new roofs in Whitehall, repaired storm damage in Easton, and inspected historic homes in Bethlehem.

We document every project, provide detailed photos, and back our work with real warranties. Our reputation depends on doing the job right the first time.

Conclusion

Your home deserves better. Trust a local roofer who knows Lehigh Valley weather, stands behind their work, and values community.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is storm chaser roofing?

It’s when out-of-town contractors follow storms, offering cheap repairs but leaving before issues appear.

Why are storm chaser roofing companies risky?

They often cut corners, don’t honor warranties, and disappear once paid.

How can I spot a storm chaser roofer?

Look for out-of-state plates, vague contracts, and high-pressure sales tactics.

What should I do if my roof is damaged after a storm?

Call a trusted local roofer for an inspection before committing to repairs.

Do storm chaser roofing crews provide real warranties?

Often, no. Even if they promise, they usually aren’t around to honor them.

How do I protect myself?

Choose a local roofer with references, licensing, and a physical office in Lehigh Valley.
